title: Export invoices in parallel without scrambling the file

blocks.text: At the end of each month the billing service writes every invoice to one file for accounting. Rendering an invoice takes a while, so it must happen on several threads at once: done one at a time, the export no longer fits in its nightly window. The writer that appends lines to the file is not thread-safe, and accounting reconciles the file line by line against the list of invoice ids, so the lines must come out in that order.

Write `export(invoiceIds, render, writer)` in `src/main/java/practice/InvoiceExport.java`. When you're done, every invoice's line is in the file, in the order of `invoiceIds`; the writer is never in use by two threads at the same time; and a slow invoice doesn't stop the others from rendering. About two lines in total.
The tests run your export on a pool of four threads.

cases.says: every invoice's line reaches the writer
the writer is never called by two threads at the same time
lines reach the writer in the order of the invoice ids, even when an early invoice finishes rendering after a later one
while one invoice is still rendering, the others are rendered

origin.section: On a Parallel Stream, forEach Calls the Consumer from Several Threads, in No Order

concepts: On a parallel stream forEach calls the Consumer from several threads at once and in no order, so a target that is not thread-safe loses elements; collect, then hand the result over from one thread, or use forEachOrdered.
